text: So what should an opponent actually prepare for? First, survive the opening without letting Barcelona dictate every decision. The early goals have been a huge part of this run. Second, defend the relationships as well as the names. Tracking Raphinha means much less if Pedri has time to pick the pass. Doubling Lamine means much less if the space you leave is immediately attacked. Third, make Barcelona defend the moments after they lose possession. Levante showed how quickly the mood can change when control slips. None of this is a magic solution. It is the task. And it explains why this team feels so difficult to plan against: you need discipline without becoming passive, pressure without losing your shape, and enough attacking threat to make Barcelona think about something other than their next move. That is a demanding ninety minutes for anybody.
